title: Complete dual-free filtrations are right orthogonal to acyclic DG modules
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}A^j$ be an associative unital differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$: $d_A$ has degree $1$, $d_A^2=0$, and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^j a\,d_A(b)$ for $a\in A^j$. A right DG $A$-module $M$ is a graded right module with a degree-$1$ differential satisfying $d_M^2=0$ and $d_M(ma)=d_M(m)a+(-1)^j m\,d_A(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Use shifts $M[k]^n=M^{n+k}$ with differential $(-1)^k d_M$ and unchanged right action. Write $(A^\vee)^n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A^{-n},\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$, with $(d\lambda)(a)=(-1)^{n+1}\lambda(d_Aa)$ for $\lambda\in(A^\vee)^n$, and right action $(\lambda a)(b)=\lambda(ab)$. Products of graded modules are taken degree by degree. Let $I=F_0I\supset F_1I\supset\cdots$ be a decreasing filtration by DG submodules. Assume the canonical map $I\to\varprojlim_{p\ge0}I/F_pI$ is an isomorphism, every quotient map $I/F_{p+1}I\to I/F_pI$ has a degree-zero right $A$-linear section after forgetting the differentials, and every layer $F_pI/F_{p+1}I$ is isomorphic as a DG module to a product of shifts of $A^\vee$. For every acyclic right DG $A$-module $C$, every degree-zero right $A$-linear chain map $g:C\to I$ admits a degree-$-1$ right $A$-linear map $h:C\to I$ with $g=d_Ih+hd_C$. Here acyclic means $\ker(d_C:C^n\to C^{n+1})=d_C(C^{n-1})$ for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 09KS, lemma-property-I-K-injective, with property (I) defined immediately before Tag 09KR, lemma-property-I-sequence; the proof uses Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free.

proof.text: The underlying character dual $C^\vee$ is acyclic. Indeed $\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ is divisible: a root of $q+\mathbf Z$ under multiplication by $m>0$ is $q/m+\mathbf Z$. Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$ and a cocycle $\lambda:C^{-r}\to\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ of degree $r$. Its cocycle equation says $\lambda d_C=0$. Since $C$ is acyclic, $\ker(d_C:C^{-r}\to C^{-r+1})=\operatorname{im}d_C^{-{r}-1}$, so $\beta(d_Cx)=(-1)^r\lambda(x)$ is a well-defined homomorphism on $\operatorname{im}d_C^{-r}$. Apply [lem-per-divisible-group-hom-extension] to its inclusion in $C^{-r+1}$ to extend $\beta$ to $\mu:C^{-r+1}\to\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$. As $\mu$ has dual degree $r-1$, $d_{C^\vee}\mu=(-1)^r\mu d_C=\lambda$. This proves acyclicity in every degree.

source.place: Tag 09KS, last sentence: exactness of character duality, expanded using the extension property for divisible abelian groups.

proof.text: For every $k\in\mathbf Z$, [lem-sfb-dg-shifted-character-dual-hom] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(C,A^\vee[k])\cong H^k(C^\vee)=0$ by Step 1. Its definition of the left side therefore supplies a degree-$-1$ right $A$-linear null-homotopy for every chain map $C\to A^\vee[k]$. This remains true with a product $\prod_{t\in T}A^\vee[k_t]$ as target: compose a chain map with every projection, choose a null-homotopy $h_t$ for each component, and define $h(c)=(h_t(c))_{t\in T}$. The differential and right action on the product are coordinatewise, so $dh+hd$ is the original map. The empty product is zero. Conjugating by each stipulated DG layer isomorphism, every chain map $C\to L_p:=F_pI/F_{p+1}I$ has such a null-homotopy.

source.place: Tags 09K4 and 09KS: vanishing for shifted dual-free modules and their products.

proof.text: Write $Q_p=I/F_pI$, $q_p:Q_{p+1}\to Q_p$, $j_p:L_p\hookrightarrow Q_{p+1}$ for the kernel inclusion, and $g_p:C\to Q_p$ for the projection of $g$. We construct degree-$-1$ right $A$-linear maps $h_p:C\to Q_p$ satisfying $d_{Q_p}h_p+h_pd_C=g_p$ and $q_ph_{p+1}=h_p$. The base is $Q_0=0$ and $h_0=0$. Given $h_p$, choose the assumed graded right $A$-linear section $s_p$ of $q_p$ and put $\widetilde h=s_ph_p$. Set $e=g_{p+1}-d_{Q_{p+1}}\widetilde h-\widetilde h d_C$. Since $q_p$ is a chain map and $q_p\widetilde h=h_p$, one has $q_pe=g_p-d_{Q_p}h_p-h_pd_C=0$. Also $d_{Q_{p+1}}e=g_{p+1}d_C-d_{Q_{p+1}}\widetilde h d_C=e d_C$, using $d^2=0$. The DG Leibniz rule makes $d\widetilde h+\widetilde h d_C$ right $A$-linear (the two terms involving $d_A(a)$ cancel). Thus $e$ factors uniquely as $j_p\epsilon_p$ for a right $A$-linear chain map $\epsilon_p:C\to L_p$.

source.place: Tag 09KS, finite filtration argument, expanded into a graded-section homotopy-lifting induction.

proof.text: By Step 2 choose $k_p:C\to L_p$ of degree $-1$ with $d_{L_p}k_p+k_pd_C=\epsilon_p$. Define $h_{p+1}=\widetilde h+j_pk_p$. As $j_p$ commutes with differentials, $d_{Q_{p+1}}h_{p+1}+h_{p+1}d_C=(g_{p+1}-j_p\epsilon_p)+j_p\epsilon_p=g_{p+1}$. Moreover $q_ph_{p+1}=q_p\widetilde h=h_p$. This completes the induction with the stated compatibility, rather than merely choosing unrelated null-homotopies on the quotients.

source.place: Tag 09KS, extension from a layer to the next quotient, explicit correction of the lifted homotopy.

proof.text: For homogeneous $c\in C^n$ the compatible tuple $(h_p(c))_{p\ge0}$ is an element of $\varprojlim_p Q_p^{n-1}$. Use the assumed canonical DG isomorphism $I\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_p Q_p$ to define its unique preimage $h(c)\in I^{n-1}$. Coordinatewise additivity and right $A$-linearity of the $h_p$ imply the same for $h$. The projection of $d_Ih+hd_C$ to $Q_p$ equals $d_{Q_p}h_p+h_pd_C=g_p$ for every $p$. Injectivity of the canonical limit map therefore gives $d_Ih+hd_C=g$. This is the required homotopy, with no boundedness or convergence of infinite sums needed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_rightLinearHomotopy_of_completeDualFreeFiltration (A : Algebra.{u}) (I : RightModule A) (_F : CompleteDualFreeFiltration A I) (C : RightModule A) (hC : ((underlying A).obj C).Acyclic) (g : C ⟶ I) : ∃ h : Homotopy ((underlying A).map g) 0, ∀ (p q : ℤ) (c : ((underlying A).obj C).X p) (a : A.X.X q), HEq (h.hom (p + q) (p + q - 1) (act A C p q c a)) (act A I (p - 1) q (h.hom p (p - 1) c) a)
